summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism teaches that people cannot mend their broken relationship with God, since sin has corrupted the conscience and captured the will, and that God saves by grace, his undeserved love given through Jesus. The proper response is repentance, turning from sin, and faith, which means believing the gospel, trusting Jesus as Savior and obeying him as Lord. Salvation brings reconciliation, forgiveness, adoption, union with Christ, new life in the Spirit and the promise of eternal life; God then transforms the believer over time. The catechism says God offers forgiveness and salvation to all people. The text read does not speak of election or of whether believers can fall away.

points.question: Can a person save themselves?
points.answer: No. Sin has corrupted the conscience and captured the will; only God can save.

points.question: How does God save?
points.answer: By grace, his undeserved love given in and through Jesus. The response is to repent and put faith in Jesus as Savior and Lord; faith means believing the gospel, entrusting oneself to him as Savior and obeying him as Lord.

points.question: Who is offered salvation?
points.answer: In his mercy God offers forgiveness and salvation from sin to all people through the life, death and resurrection of Jesus.

review.note: Questions 1-18 and 133-134 read in the 2016 draft on 2026-11-12; the approved 2020 edition may differ. "Offered to all" is our reading: the catechism says salvation is offered to all but does not discuss election or whether response is part of God's plan. The ACNA also holds the Articles of Religion, whose Articles XI and XVII are the Church of England's and were not used for this row. Not yet checked by a second reviewer.
